text:
jordan: Quick bench summary — ran a focused prefills+decode sweep for Llama-2-7b and Mistral-7b on A100 vs H100 across us-west1 / eu-west1. Unexpected: H100 shows a higher decode p95 on Llama-2-7b at low QPS in us-west1. Full raw numbers below + cost calc. gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/bench-1725607890 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

perfbot: Automated job uploaded results -> ci/bench/1725607890 (artifacts + csv).

sophia: Can you paste the compact table here? want tokens/sec and $/1M tokens for quick triage.

jordan: Paste of the key rows (single-run median, p95 decode, cost normalized to $/1M tokens assuming on-demand prices we use):

```
model            | gpu  | region    | prefill_ms | decode_p95_ms | tokens_per_sec | $/1M_tokens | kernel_hint
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Llama-2-7b       | A100 | us-west1  | 180        | 9             | 7,500          | $14.2       | cutlass
Llama-2-7b       | H100 | us-west1  | 165        | 12            | 8,900          | $17.1       | cuBLAS-fallback
Mistral-7b       | A100 | us-west1  | 210        | 10            | 6,600          | $15.5       | cutlass
Mistral-7b       | H100 | us-west1  | 170        | 8             | 11,000         | $12.6       | flash_attn
Llama-2-7b (int8)| A100 | eu-west1  | 190        | 10            | 8,200          | $9.8        | cutlass+int8
Llama-2-7b (int8)| H100 | eu-west1  | 160        | 11            | 9,600          | $11.5       | flash_attn+int8
```

jordan: Notes: 1) The Llama-2-7b H100 row (us-west1) shows worse decode p95 despite higher tokens/sec — appears to be taily at low concurrency which matches a kernel fallthrough during short-decoding microbatches. 2) Mistral benefits a lot from flash_attn on H100 (much higher tokens/sec). 3) int8 quant helps cost massively but kernel support varies by model/GPU combo.

miguel: Reproduced locally — when the runtime selects cuBLAS path for the attention (fallback) we see more p95 variance. Re-run command I used: 

``
./bench_runner --model llama-2-7b --gpu h100 --region us-west1 --qps 2 --batch-size 1 --seq 512 --trace kernels --out artifacts/1725607890
```

miguel: Attached trace shows attention kernel choosing cuBLAS matmul for k/v sizes under 32 due to our current kernel-picker cost model.

sophia: So there's a selector bug? or cost model wrong for short sequences on H100?

miguel: Seems like cost model assumes cuBLAS is cheaper for tiny kernels on H100 but flash_attn actually wins for our microbatch decode pattern. Need to tweak heuristics. I can push a flag to force flash_attn for decode path in runtime.

ciara: Regional note — eu-west1 numbers are cleaner (less tail) for Llama-2-7b on H100. Might be due to different NIC/placement or different microcode/driver versions on the pool we used. We should verify driver versions.

jordan: Driver/stack: both pools reported CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.18, but eu-west1 h100 uses OFA v2. US-west1 h100 nodes had a slightly older firmware (ticketed to infra).

miguel: Quick config snippet to force flash_attn for decode (temp):

```
# runtime override (dev/test only)
REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=flash_attn \
REDWOOD_KERNEL_FILTER=decode_only \
./redwood_runtime --model-config models/llama-2-7b.json --serve
```

miguel: After forcing flash_attn locally, p95 dropped from 12ms -> 7.5ms and tokens/sec stayed ~9k. So we can recover tail by adjusting selector.

sophia: Nice. For cost calc: curious why $/1M for H100 Llama is higher even with better throughput in some rows. Assumptions?

jordan: We used list-like on-demand hourly rates: A100 $3.2/hr, H100 $5.8/hr (our procurement). So even with higher tokens/sec, the higher H100 hourly makes $/1M not automatically smaller unless tokens/sec advantage > price ratio. Mistral on H100 wins economically because flash_attn yields ~1.6x tokens/sec.

ciara: Action items: 1) Miguel to adjust kernel cost model + run a 1/4/8 concurrency sweep. 2) Infra to check h100 firmware in us-west1 (I opened INF-2341). 3) Re-run the quantized suite (int8,4-bit) with the new selector and compare quality baselines.

miguel: I'll land a quick toggle in runtime and queue bench job (tag: bench-1725607890-retry). Command I'll use to sweep: 

``
for q in 1 4 8; do 
  ./bench_runner --model llama-2-7b --gpu h100 --region us-west1 --qps $q --batch-size 1 --seq 512 --kernel-override flash_attn 
done
```

deploy-bot: Bench job queued: bench-1725607890-retry (ETA ~45m).

jordan: Plan: once we have the re-run, we'll update the model catalog performance profile and recommend kernel defaults per model+gpu. Also add a rubric for quantization compatibility notes (int8 fallback behavior).

sophia: Can someone add a small note to the onboarding doc about "kernel fragility at low QPS" so solutions engineers know the gotcha?

ciara: Will add a short blurb and link to this thread + INF-2341.

jordan: Thanks — will follow up with final CSV + recommended defaults when bench-1725607890-retry finishes.
